questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to an English-speaking country, outside Europe, and to a place where it is warm

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find the informations

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university offered free airport transportation when I arrived. We also had an introduction day with a barbecue and social events, where there was an opportunity to get to know other exchange students

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The introduction day could have been better organized, but it was nice to meet other exchange students that day

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy, as I knew someone who had previously been on exchange in Sydney, and I got the contact information through her

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very nice to live in Coogee. It is close to University and close to the beach. It is expensive to live in Sydney

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived in a house with 30 other exchange students. It was very nice to have a sense of community and people around you. It ensured that you were always surrounded by others

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The website seemed very old and slow, but it worked with some patience

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First, you had to apply for approval to take certain courses. Later, you had to enroll in the courses through another portal. There, you needed to adjust your schedule and secure your spot before all places were taken.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I didn’t use any assistance, so I’m not sure. However, from my experience, they respond to emails quite quickly

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got a spot in all the courses I applied for. However, due to some scheduling conflicts, I couldn’t get all of my first-choice courses. I decided to switch a course at the last minute and still got a place, so in the end, I got everything I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It’s smart to apply for approval for all the courses you are considering, as it makes it easier later when you need to apply for a final spot in the course. You can only apply for a course once you have received approval to do so.  It took some effort to figure out and get the schedule to work, especially if you want flexibility and fewer school days.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The program is structured so that you take one course during their Winter Term, which lasts 3–4 weeks. After that, you take three courses during Term 3. Having a slow and easy start with just one course worked well. The Winter Term is usually only for exchange students, so it’s a good way to meet other exchange students

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took mostly beginner to intermediate courses, combining practical skills and foundational theory in humanities, design, and economics. The level was easier than UCPH. Much easier to get higher grades

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I took a mix of design and economics courses. The economics courses were similar to UCPH, with lectures and tutorials. The design courses were more like high school classes, where you sit in a classroom, are taught something, and then work on it practically

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: HUMS1010, DDES1043, DDES1150, ECON1202

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked all my courses. They were very different from each other, and I enjoyed trying something other than the typical economics and computer science courses. I liked DDES1043, as it taught me skills in publication design that I will always be able to use. But I also liked ECON1202, where we went a bit more in-depth into basic mathematics within economics

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The student-visa was expensive. They also require you to have health insurance in Australia, which also costs around 1,700 DKK. The university helps you with this

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Travel around was expensive. The prices are around the same as in Denmark. Groceries were on the expensive side. Tak-away a little less expensive as expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were so many options, with lots of different clubs you could join. I never got around to it, but I wish I had

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you could possibly dream of. There were so many clubs, covering everything from sports to matcha

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a club. I never did, but I wish I had. It helps you build a bigger network

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around Australia. It’s a huge country with so much to offer, featuring very diverse cultures and landscapes. I loved every place I visited

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, and the culture is very Western and somewhat similar to Denmark

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It wasn’t easy to start conversations with the locals, as there are many international students. I found it easier in courses where I didn’t know anyone, as that encouraged me to talk with local students, both international and domestic

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any. The biggest difference is that Australians live a very active lifestyle in the mornings, with activities already in full swing from 6 am

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated the work-life balance, as many Australians prioritize free time and social life, which is inspiring compared to more stressful environments

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Live in Coogee (close to the Beach)
- Find a good balance between freedom and school, you’ll manage to get through your studies
- Take courses that seem manageable and interesting to you

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university is easy to get in touch with and provides good information from start to finish. You don’t need to worry too much about the university. Lecturers are friendly, and help is always available

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I think the most rewarding part was creating my own everyday life in a completely new country. It was fun to experience a different university and see how it operated

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I found it an easy country to be in, and it was easy to communicate with people because they spoke English. I don’t think I faced any major challenges in that regard

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
